name: Teleporters
description: There are $$$n+1$$$ teleporters on a straight line, located in points $$$0$$$, $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, $$$a_3$$$, ..., $$$a_n$$$. It's possible to teleport from point $$$x$$$ to point $$$y$$$ if there are teleporters in both of those points, and it costs $$$(x-y)^2$$$ energy. You want to install some additional teleporters so that it is possible to get from the point $$$0$$$ to the point $$$a_n$$$ (possibly through some other teleporters) spending no more than $$$m$$$ energy in total. Each teleporter you install must be located in an integer point . What is the minimum number of teleporters you have to install?
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_1 \lt a_2 \lt a_3 \lt \dots \lt a_n \le 10^9$$$). The third line contains one integer $$$m$$$ ($$$a_n \le m \le 10^{18}$$$).
output_specification: Print one integer — the minimum number of teleporters you have to install so that it is possible to get from $$$0$$$ to $$$a_n$$$ spending at most $$$m$$$ energy. It can be shown that it's always possible under the constraints from the input format.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1661F — Teleporters [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
